newsitem.title: LATVIA: ESTONIA-SWEDBANK SEES GROWTH, FOREIGN DEFICIT WORRY.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-SWEDBANK SEES GROWTH, FOREIGN DEFICIT WORRY.

text.p: Swedbank said on Tuesaday that Estonia had reasonably good growth prospects but had worries about its about foreign trade deficit.
Gross domestic product (GDP) growth was expected to be on last year's level at four percent, Swedbank said in an analysis of eastern Europe, including the Baltic states.
Estonia showed a close-to-balanced budget although a big current account deficit was a worrying factor, Swedbank said.
Estonia's imports grew in 1996 by 30 percent while exports were up 20 percent only, which has resulted in a current account deficit of six percent of the GDP.
"A tangible increase in the export-oriented sectors is needed to close the gap as well as a better service sector balance," Swedbank said in the report.
It said that the introduction of import tarifs on agricultural products was a sign of political insecurity.
"It would cost the state budget more than it would bring in by way of income and would hardly be in the interests of the consumers," Swedbank added.
It added in the analysis that portfolio investment in Estonia has increased a great deal and that foreign capital accounts for some 40 percent of Tallinn bourse turnover.
